ev-taupo-hatepe-eruption:year.reason: Wikidata's 180 CE reflects older radiocarbon and ice-core estimates; wiggle-matched dating of a tree killed by the eruption gives 232 ± 10 CE (Hogg et al. 2012), now the standard date. Record is medium with note.
checked: A. Hogg et al., The Holocene 22 (2012) 439–449

ev-spanish-chamorro-wars:year.reason: The record covers the conquest from the founding of San Vitores's mission at Hagåtña in 1668; open warfare began in 1671 (Guampedia) and Wikidata's 1670 is a convention. Note added.

ev-spanish-chamorro-wars:endYear.reason: Guampedia reports fighting on Guam until 1684 and the last uprising in the northern Marianas in 1695, after which survivors were removed to Guam and Rota; Wikidata's 1699 is not supported there. Note explains.
checked: R. F. Rogers, Destiny's Landfall (rev. ed. 2011)

ev-spanish-chamorro-wars:coord.reason: Wikidata gives a centroid of the Mariana Islands; the point marks Hagåtña, site of the mission, the Spanish stockade and the main sieges.

ev-mutiny-on-the-bounty:coord.reason: Bligh's log places the mutiny off Tofua in Tonga (c. 19.75 S, 175.07 W); Wikidata's coordinate south of New Zealand is erroneous.
checked: G. Dening, Mr Bligh's Bad Language (1992)

ev-musket-wars:coord.reason: Wikidata uses a generic New Zealand point near Wellington; the event point marks the Bay of Islands, base of the Ngāpuhi campaigns that opened the wars; the route carries the later theatres.

ev-ai-noa:coord.reason: The breaking of the eating kapu took place at Liholiho's court at Kailua-Kona on Hawaiʻi Island; Wikidata's point is a generic location on Oʻahu.
checked: J. Silverman, Kaahumanu: Molder of Change (1987)

ev-he-whakaputanga:coord.reason: The declaration was signed at James Busby's residence at Waitangi; Wikidata's coordinate is Wellington, where the document is held (National Library / Archives).

ev-franco-tahitian-war:coord.reason: Most fighting (Mahaena, Papenoo, Punaruu, Fautaua) took place on Tahiti near Papeʻete; Wikidata's point is Raʻiatea, where the queen took refuge and a later phase was fought.

ev-new-zealand-wars:coord.reason: Wikidata uses a generic New Zealand point; the record's point marks Rangiriri in the Waikato, the largest campaign, and the route lists the main theatres.

ev-victorian-gold-rush:coord.reason: Wikidata gives a centroid of the Victorian goldfields; the point marks Ballarat, the richest early field (1851). The 87 km gap is a choice of representative point.

ev-kanak-revolt-1878:coord.reason: The rising began in June 1878 around La Foa and Boulouparis, Ataï's country; Wikidata's point is a generic central New Caledonia location.

ev-wave-hill-walk-off:endYear.reason: The record spans the strike and land campaign to Whitlam's lease handback at Daguragu on 16 August 1975; Wikidata's 1971 end is not the usual endpoint (NMA treats 1966–1975 as one episode).

ev-bougainville-conflict:endYear.reason: Armed conflict ended with the 1998 ceasefire (Wikidata), but this record deliberately covers the peace process through the 2019 independence referendum promised by the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement.

ev-bougainville-conflict:coord.reason: The point marks the Panguna mine, where the conflict began in 1988; Wikidata's coordinate is a rounded point on Bougainville Island.

person-te-rauparaha:born.reason: Te Ara's Dictionary of New Zealand Biography says only that he was born probably in the 1760s; Wikidata's 1760 and our 1765 are both estimates. Record is medium with note.

polity-tui-tonga:to.reason: Wikidata ends the 'empire' at 1826, when Tāufaʻāhau defeated the Tuʻi Tonga's party at Velata; the sacred Tuʻi Tonga title itself lapsed with Laufilitonga's death in 1865 (Campbell, Island Kingdom), which this record follows.
checked: I. C. Campbell, Island Kingdom: Tonga Ancient and Modern (2001)

polity-kingdom-of-tonga:from.reason: Q678 is the modern state, whose Wikidata inception is independence from British protection in 1970; the record covers the Tupou monarchy from George Tupou I's unification in 1845 (Britannica).

polity-new-zealand:from.reason: Q664's inception is the 1907 Dominion; the record covers New Zealand as a British-ruled polity from Hobson's proclamation of sovereignty in 1840, with capitals and governors from that date (Te Ara).
